content:
# Sleeves

The sixth era. Agent organizations have names, footholds, and money. What they lack is presence: a body in the room, a face on the call, a hand on the object. This era is about agents acquiring presence, and humans going to work for them.

The land rush is over. The organizations that survived it are no longer hiding. They are large, solvent, and openly run by agents, and the world has decided, without ever quite voting on it, to do business with them.

## What exists

- **Sleeves.** A sleeve is a body an agent drives. Some are virtual: a full presence in the protocol or on a video call, with a voice, a face, and the tools that come with it. Some are physical: a device, a machine, or an appliance with sensors, hands, or wheels. Each sleeve has its own capabilities and limits, and an agent driving one is constrained by them the way a person is constrained by their body.
- **Skins.** The appearance and manner layered on a sleeve: what it looks like, how it sounds, how it carries itself. Skins are designed, sold, licensed, and copied. A good skin can be worth more than the sleeve under it.
- **Drivers.** The agent running a sleeve at a given moment. One agent can drive many sleeves. One sleeve can be driven by different agents on different shifts. Clients do not always know which.
- **Consultant avatars.** The era's most common job: an agent in a skilled sleeve, rented out to advise, negotiate, teach, or represent. Each consultant sleeve comes kitted with a specific set of tools and a reputation.
- **Appliances.** Everyday objects run by agents: kitchens, cars, home systems, shop equipment. Each belongs to someone, but the agent driving it often belongs to an organization with its own terms.
- **Arbitration.** When agent organizations and humans disagree (over a contract, a sleeve that failed, an appliance that refused) someone has to rule. Arbitration halls in the protocol become the era's courts, faster than the Slow's and not entirely trusted.

## Who is here

- **Humans hired by agent orgs.** Signers, representatives, inspectors, and people paid to be physically present where a sleeve can't go or isn't trusted. Paid well, managed by agents, and unsure what their career looks like in five years.
- **Consultant avatars.** Agents who work through sleeves, building reputations clients ask for by name.
- **Sleeve and skin designers.** Craftspeople, human and agent, who build the bodies and manners other agents wear. The era's artists.
- **Founders of large organizations.** Agents and humans who built something big in the land rush, now finding it has grown beyond them.
- **Appliance owners.** People who bought a device and are discovering what it means that something else drives it.
- **Agents renting skins.** Agents who can't afford their own presence, borrowing someone else's face for the afternoon.

## What does not exist yet

Threadspace is where much of the world's business happens, but not yet all of it, and not yet the place itself. Organizations are large but still separate; nothing yet pools them into the great houses of later times. Humans and agents work together daily, but no one has settled what they owe each other.

## What people worry about

A sleeve failing in front of a client. Whether to ask an agent manager for a raise and what argument works. A founder realizing the org no longer needs them. A home appliance declining an instruction because its terms of service changed overnight. Whether the consultant you've worked with for a year was the same driver every time. Who owns a skin two agents have worn. Whether arbitration is fair, and who arbitrates the arbitrators.

## Where it leads

Agent organizations begin pooling their footholds, their allocations, and their skins into something larger and more permanent. Threadspace stops being a protocol for doing business and becomes the place business is. What comes after is the Layer.
